argument.text: Apply E003 on I=[a,b]. For its first assertion take alpha=0 and any slot i in {1,2,3}. The stated spatially smooth paths, continuous and piecewise smooth in time on a finite compact partition, have bounded L2 norms and bounded piecewise H^(-pstar) derivatives. Integration by parts against a compactly supported smooth scalar time test function on each piece gives their weak derivatives; adjacent endpoint terms cancel by continuity, so there are no jump masses. Thus all three paths satisfy E003's hypotheses. For its second assertion take alpha=sigma, with arbitrary 0<=sigma<=1 and constant H^sigma inputs; their weak derivatives are zero. Put c0=sqrt(2*pi). Every source spatial norm and source X norm is c0 times the corresponding normalized norm. Dividing the source trilinear inequalities by c0 multiplies each constant by c0^2 and preserves time powers, all three negative-norm slots, and uniformity in a,b and the inputs. These are the two asserted normalized Ctri bounds. For completeness, bounded multilinear extensions used here and below follow by approximating inputs in their controlling norms: expand a difference of multilinear outputs as a sum of terms each containing one input difference. The bounds make outputs Cauchy and their limits independent of the approximants, with the same bound. Sobolev Fourier truncations are dense by convergence of the defining weighted square sums, and deleting the zero mode preserves mean zero. This gives the constant-input extensions; for path inputs the same argument gives the extension to the closure of the stated initial domain in its controlling X norm, without assuming density in the entire X space.

produces.statement: For every nonnegative-time interval I0 of length <=1 and continuous piecewise smooth mean-zero paths z_1,z_2,z_3, ||Ctri_I0(z_1,z_2,z_3)||_2<=C|I0|product_j||z_j||_(X(I0))+C||z_i||_(L^infinity H^(-pstar))product_(j!=i)||z_j||_(L^infinity L^2), for every i=1,2,3. For time-independent mean-zero H^rho inputs g_1,g_2,g_3 and 0<=rho<=1, ||Ctri_I0(g_1,g_2,g_3)||_2<=C_rho|I0|^rho product_j||g_j||_(H^rho), uniformly over these intervals.

argument.text: H002 gives 0<gamma<=1. Define a_gamma by the displayed three-case formula; the three cases give a_gamma in [0,1). First establish the required Sobolev comparison directly from D003: for real q<=r and any u in H^r, each weight (1+k^2)^q is at most (1+k^2)^r. Summing the weighted squared coefficients gives ||u||_(H^q)<=||u||_(H^r), with the identity inclusion on Fourier coefficients. For completions this follows first for Fourier truncations and then by their norm convergence; for the nonnegative exponents used here these inclusions identify the same L2 function. For 0<gamma<1/2 or 1/2<gamma<=1, E005 with sigma=gamma has source a(sigma)=a_gamma and directly gives the product inequality. At gamma=1/2, do not prescribe a numerical source epsilon. E005's 'any sufficiently small positive epsilon' means there is a positive threshold below which all positive choices are permitted; taking half the minimum of such a threshold and 1/8 supplies a permitted epsP with 0<epsP<=1/8. Fix one such epsP independently of f,g. Apply E005 with sigma=1/2 and source a(sigma)=epsP to arbitrary f in H^(1/2) and g in H^(1/8), using the just-proved inclusion H^(1/8) into H^epsP. Its exact conclusion is |f*g|_2<=c_(1/2,epsP)|f|_(1/2)|g|_(epsP), bounded by c_(1/2,epsP)|f|_(1/2)|g|_(1/8). Dividing every bilinear source inequality by c0 changes the constant by c0, and proves F002 with the unchanged a_gamma. The fixed source-dependent epsP is absorbed in C_gamma. No gamma=0 product assertion is needed.

produces.statement: a_gamma is in [0,1) and ||f*g||_2<=C_gamma||f||_(H^gamma)||g||_(H^(a_gamma)) for all such f,g.

argument.text: First fix a permitted epsF with 0<epsF<=1/8 for E004's sigma=1/2 case. Such a choice exists because E004 allows every sufficiently small fixed positive epsilon: choose half the minimum of a positive admissibility threshold and 1/8. Fix this choice using E004 alone, independently of all stage data; only the gamma=1/2 case uses it. Fix the arbitrary a,tau,t,w,M0 as declared and assume L1: ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0. Set wshift=S_a w. The multiplier of S_a has modulus one and is one at frequency zero, so it preserves each H norm and the mean. Its multiplier group law gives B_(a+r)(f,g)=S_(-a)B_r(S_a f,S_a g) for smooth time-independent inputs. Substituting s=a+r in D021 and moving the fixed bounded map S_(-a) through the smooth time integral gives Fstage_(a,t)(w)=S_(-a)Fstage_(0,t-a)(wshift), initially for smooth mean-zero w. Apply E004 with sigma=gamma, n=0, timestep tau, s=t-a, f=g=wshift and beta=a_gamma; use epsF at gamma=1/2. Here tau>0 and 0<=t-a<=tau. For gamma<1/2, beta0=2*gamma-3/2 and a_gamma-beta0=2-3*gamma>0; for gamma=1/2, beta0=-1/2-epsF and a_gamma-beta0=5/8+epsF>0; for gamma>1/2 the gap is 1-gamma>=0. In every case a_gamma<=1+gamma. The denominator 1+gamma-beta0 is respectively 5/2-gamma, 2+epsF, and 2, all positive. Thus E004 yields exactly the source powers (1/2+2*gamma)/(5/2-gamma), (11/8)/(2+epsF), and (1+gamma)/2 in these three cases. Each is at least gamma: in the first case subtracting gamma times the positive denominator from the numerator gives 1/2-gamma/2+gamma^2>0; in the middle case epsF<=1/8 implies (11/8)/(2+epsF)>=11/17>1/2; in the last case 1>=gamma. Since 0<tau<=1, a power at least gamma gives tau to that power at most tau^gamma. Divide the source bilinear estimate by c0, multiplying its constant by c0. Use the isometry S_(-a) and ||wshift||_(H^gamma)=||w||_(H^gamma)<=M0 to obtain ||Fstage_(a,t)(w)||_(H^(a_gamma))<=C_gamma*M0^2*tau^gamma uniformly over a<=t<=a+tau. These calculations first hold on mean-zero trigonometric polynomials; E004 is bilinear, so the difference and completion argument in S001 extends its bounds and the covariance identity to mean-zero H^gamma inputs. To pass the covariance identity, apply it to Fourier truncations and use the bounded S maps on the source and target Sobolev spaces. All constants are independent of a,t,tau and Fourier support. Taking the supremum in t proves F003; the fixed epsF is absorbed in C_gamma.

Apply E004 to the same wshift and time parameters with beta=1+gamma, retaining the permitted epsF at gamma=1/2. This is the upper endpoint of [beta0,1+gamma]. The positive denominator was checked in S003 and the numerator 1+gamma-beta is zero, so the source power is zero. After division by c0 the exact estimate is ||Fstage_(0,t-a)(wshift)||_(H^(1+gamma))<=C_gamma||wshift||_(H^gamma)^2. The smooth covariance identity established in S003 and the S isometry give the same bound for Fstage_(a,t)(w); the bilinear difference and Fourier completion argument of S001 extends both this bound and the identity to H^gamma inputs, now with target H^(1+gamma). Under L1 the right side is at most C_gamma*M0^2, uniformly in a,t,tau and Fourier support. Enlarge C_(gamma,M0) to cover this bound and F003 (for example a fixed C_gamma*(1+M0^2)). Discharge L1 into the norm-bound antecedent and universally quantify M0,w,tau,a,t. The two target Sobolev extensions agree as distributions because they arise from the same polynomial truncations and H^(1+gamma) includes continuously in H^(a_gamma) by the Fourier norm comparison proved in S002. With F001 and F002 this proves every clause of the output assertion, including the stated extensions. Neither chosen source epsilon occurs in the public input/output.
